question: Iron armor made undersea telegraph cables stronger. Why did it make signals worse?
answer: Iron armor made the undersea telegraph cable stronger, but it made the signal worse. Iron is a good conductor, so when it was wrapped around the insulated core, the cable acted like a capacitor. That raised the line's capacitance and hindered the electromagnetic fields that carry the signal. This is why most power lines today hang high in the air.
move: A conductor close to a wire adds capacitance and hinders the signal.
